title: Existence of the exceptional inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ be admissible: $A$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Use the pro-étale coefficient categories and $\Dctf$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and the localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For a chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper ([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]), let $Rf_!$ be the restriction of $Rp_*D(j_!)$ to these closures, with the module-object coefficient convention of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Then the exact coproduct-preserving functor
$$
Rf_!:\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))
$$
has an exact right adjoint
$$
f^!:\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda)),\qquad
\Hom(Rf_!M,N)\simeq\Hom(M,f^!N),
$$
naturally for every $M\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ and $N\in\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. It is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the adjunction, and it preserves arbitrary set-indexed direct sums.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ and $\mathcal D=\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. By [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses], both are locally small triangulated categories with arbitrary direct sums, and small skeletons of their $\Dctf$ subcategories are compact generating sets. The standing finite-type separated schemes are qcqs: finite type includes quasi-compactness, and separatedness makes the diagonal a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact. Nagata [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] therefore supplies $f=p\circ j$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper. For this compactification, [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] says exactly that $F=Rp_*D(j_!):\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is exact, preserves direct sums and sends $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. This is the $Rf_!$ fixed in the statement.

source.place: First paragraph: the Brown hypotheses and exact, coproduct-preserving lower shriek; compactification input is det-sf-comp-coherence-single.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint] to $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Its hypotheses are precisely those established in step 1: set-indexed coproducts in both categories, compact generation of $\mathcal C$, exactness of $F$, and preservation of coproducts by $F$. It gives a functor $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ with $F\dashv G$. Write $f^!=G$, let $\varepsilon_N:FGN\to N$ be the counit, and use the natural adjunction bijections $\Hom_{\mathcal D}(FM,N)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal C}(M,GN)$. This is a single Brown application on $\mathcal C$, not on the whole ambient pro-étale derived category.

source.place: Tag 0A8G, proposition-brown: Brown representability gives a right adjoint.

proof.text:
The adjunction determines the shift structure on $G$. For every integer $n$, the natural chain
$$\Hom(M,GN[n])\cong\Hom(M[-n],GN)\cong\Hom(F(M[-n]),N)\cong\Hom(FM,N[n])\cong\Hom(M,G(N[n]))$$
uses the shift structure of the exact functor $F$. The chain and its inverse are natural in $M$; [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] therefore gives mutually inverse maps $GN[n]\cong G(N[n])$. The same naturality calculation for $n,m$ shows that the map for $n+m$ equals the composite of the maps for $n$ and $m$, so these are coherent shifts. Equivalently, the map $GN[1]\to G(N[1])$ is the transpose of
$$F(GN[1])\cong F(GN)[1]\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_N[1]}N[1].$$
By the transpose formula, its counit square commutes. For the unit, transpose both composites from $M[1]$ to $G(FM)[1]$ and to $G(F(M[1]))$; the counit square and the two triangle identities reduce both transposes to the identity of $F(M)[1]$, so the unit square commutes. Thus the hypotheses, including adjunction-compatible coherent shifts, of [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] hold, and that lemma makes $G$ exact.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; canonical shift structure before applying exactness.

proof.text: If $J$ is any other right adjoint of $F$, with counit $\varepsilon^J$, apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Its component $\gamma_N:GN\to JN$ is the $J$-transpose of $\varepsilon_N$; its inverse is the $G$-transpose of $\varepsilon^J_N$. The cited statement asserts that these components are natural, mutually inverse and the only counit-compatible family. Hence the adjoint is unique up to the unique adjunction-compatible natural isomorphism claimed.

Let $(N_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ be any set-indexed family in $\mathcal D$, let $\iota_\alpha:N_\alpha\to\bigoplus_\alpha N_\alpha$ be its coprojections, and let $\theta:\bigoplus_\alpha GN_\alpha\to G(\bigoplus_\alpha N_\alpha)$ have restriction $G\iota_\alpha$ on each summand. Choose a small skeleton $S_X$ of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. For $P\in S_X$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, $P[n]$ lies in $\Dctf$ because that category is thick, hence it is isomorphic to an object of $S_X$ and is compact by [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses]; compactness is invariant under isomorphism. By [det-sf-comp-coherence-single], $F(P[n])\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, so it is likewise isomorphic to a skeleton object and compact in $\mathcal D$. Using the defining bijections of compactness [def-pc-compact-object] and adjunction gives
$$\Hom(P[n],\bigoplus_\alpha GN_\alpha)\cong\bigoplus_\alpha\Hom(P[n],GN_\alpha)\cong\bigoplus_\alpha\Hom(F(P[n]),N_\alpha)\cong\Hom(F(P[n]),\bigoplus_\alpha N_\alpha)\cong\Hom(P[n],G(\bigoplus_\alpha N_\alpha)).$$
This composite is exactly $\Hom(P[n],\theta)$: on an element $a:P[n]\to GN_\alpha$, naturality of the adjunction sends $G\iota_\alpha\circ a$ to $\iota_\alpha\circ\varepsilon_{N_\alpha}\circ F(a)$. These are the maps defining the displayed compactness bijections. Therefore postcomposition by $\theta$ is bijective on every shifted generator.

source.place: Second paragraph: compact-generator Hom calculation, with the canonical map checked on each coprojection.

proof.text: Complete $\theta:A\to B$ to a distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{\theta}B\to C\to A[1]$ in $\mathcal C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and its shifted/rotated instances, the sequence $\Hom(P[n],A)\to\Hom(P[n],B)\to\Hom(P[n],C)\to\Hom(P[n],A[1])\to\Hom(P[n],B[1])$ is exact. The first and last arrows are bijective by step 5 (the last is the $n-1$ test). Thus $\Hom(P[n],C)=0$ for every $P,n$. The explicit zero-detection assertion of [det-brown-hypotheses-generation] gives $C=0$. Finally [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $\theta$ an isomorphism. The empty indexing set is included: all Hom groups in step 5 are zero and the same cone argument applies. Hence $G=f^!$ preserves every set-indexed direct sum.
